Man Buys 2025 Aston Martin DBX707 for $318,500, Drives 6,600 Miles, Sells for $197,000
22 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
To think that you go through the trouble of spending over $300,000 on an SUV, only to then sell it a year later for $121,500 under MSRP. That's about as brutal a hit as you can take on a luxury car, and it goes to show just what the market "thinks" about the DBX707 and Aston Martin as a brand. Overpriced and overvalued. Sorry, but here's all the proof you need.
While this car isn't a delivery miles example, it's not particularly high-mileage either. It was driven only 6,600 miles since new, which points to it having been a weekend getaway car or a family vacation car. Still, it lost 38.15% of its original value in the blink of an eye. The owner basically paid almost $19 per mile to drive this car. This type of math hurts my brain. At this point, just get a G-Wagen, because it's the only SUV that's unusually resistant to depreciation.
Fine, you want something quicker than a G-Class, alright, no problem. How about the Urus Performante? It too will hold on to its original value a lot better than a DBX707.
Anyway, let's say you want this DBX707 in particular. Let's take a closer look at the spec, starting with the Neutron White colorway, itself a $13k option. Other exterior highlights include the panoramic sunroof, LED exterior lighting, a 360-degree camera system, power-folding heated mirrors, quad exhaust outlets, a receiver hitch, power-operated tailgate, plus a set of 23" Fortis forged wheels with Pirelli rubber and red-finished calipers over carbon-ceramic discs.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the Onyx Black and Light Argento Metallic leather seats (heated/ventilated), a color-coordinated dashboard, center console, and door panels, but also carbon fiber trim accents, a Bowers & Wilkins sound system, heated rear seats, keyless entry, red seat belts, three-zone automatic climate control, adaptive cruise control, Apple CarPlay Ultra, Android Auto, and a heated steering wheel, among other things.
I actually don't mind the spec at all. The interior is wicked nice, and the Neutron White exterior colorway is very clean, very modern. This makes the depreciation even worse if you think about it. This is about as nice a DBX707 as you can find, and still you're paying crazy amounts out of pocket just to drive this thing to the store, in terms of depreciation.
Photo: Bring a Trailer It's cars like this that make people buy a luxury watch instead, like a crazy nice Patek or an RM. Those will hold their value infinitely better than just about anything with four wheels coming out of Great Britain.
Last but not least, let's talk about that twin-turbo V8 . I already mentioned the power at 697 hp (707 ps), with everything going to all four wheels via a nine-speed automatic transmission. This thing will get you from zero to 60 mph (97 kph) in about 3.1 seconds, which is crazy-fast for an SUV.
